channel.title: The ArmChair Journal - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The ArmChair Journal (armchairjournal.com)

item.title: Free-riders of Freedom: Political parties
item.description: Cash transfers are on the rise in India, compromising capital expenditures. Using game theory, political parties can be modelled in an externalities problem.

item.title: Sino-Taiwan tensions and India’s strategic dilemma
item.description: One-fifth of global maritime trade goes through Taiwan Strait. Amidst One China Policy and unofficial relations with Taiwan, India must ensure its tech supply chains are secure.

item.title: Coaching Classrooms, Or what do you call a group of parrots?
item.description: Under the lure of a good life, coaching centres in India exploit the dreams of parents and put students into cages that can’t dream

item.title: Learning in an Unfamiliar Tongue? Reflections from a Delhi School
item.description: Most Indian schools have children who have different mother-tongues compared to medium of instruction posing unique learning challenges to policymakers.

item.title: Great power rush in melting Arctic: Where does India stand?
item.description: Melting ice in the arctic and possibilities of energy resources has led to the US, Russia and China recalibrating their arctic positing. India must play a role too.

item.title: Western democracies on the edge? Polarisation, protests, and the battle for legitimacy
item.description: Western democracies have been seeing a crisis of legitimacy as citizens are not trusting institutions and governments anymore. What would this lead to?

item.title: Neither Law nor Liberation: Maoism in Adivasi India
item.description: Home Minister Amit Shah promised to eliminate Naxalism by 2026, the Communist Party of India (Maoist) appears to be in steep decline.

item.title: Rebellious women: Whose JNU after all?
item.description: JNU’s women students who drove the university’s success now face adversity: first, because they are women; second, because they are women of JNU.

item.title: Power, Poetry, and Protest: Churchill, Tagore, and Gandhi in the Early Twentieth Century
item.description: Rabindranath Tagore, Winston Churchill and Mahatma Gandhi: Each of them shaped the politics of their times and continue to stay relevant even today.

item.title: Sacred Stereotypes: How AI turns Faith into Fear
item.description: Usage of Artificial Intelligence to scale religious propaganda is exaggerated through fabricating evidence by AI-generated videos and photographs.
